nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong desert sun drives plant growth, though heat and dryness limit how much of it plants can use.

nodes.name: Scarce rain and flash floods
nodes.desc: The park averages only about 200 mm of precipitation a year. Late-summer storms bring most of it, often as sudden flash floods.

nodes.name: Biological soil crust
nodes.desc: A living skin of cyanobacteria, fungi, lichen, moss and algae that protects sandy desert soil from erosion.

nodes.name: Two-needle pinyon
nodes.desc: A small pine of the dry woodlands, with large seeds eaten by birds and rodents. Drought and insects can kill stands.

nodes.name: Utah juniper
nodes.desc: Grows with pinyon in the pinyon-juniper woodland that covers much of the Colorado Plateau.

nodes.name: Stansbury cliffrose
nodes.desc: A woody desert shrub. Wikipedia lists cliffrose among the plants mule deer commonly browse.

nodes.name: Cliff prickly-pear
nodes.desc: A low, spiny cactus that stores water in its pads. Bighorn sheep break open cacti when grass is scarce.

nodes.name: Indian ricegrass
nodes.desc: A native bunchgrass of sandy soils on the Colorado Plateau, grazed by hoofed animals.

nodes.name: Mule deer
nodes.desc: A browser that eats mostly shrubs and trees, with some forbs, grass and fruit. Coyotes and cougars hunt it.

nodes.name: Bighorn sheep
nodes.desc: Lives on steep rocky ground. Eats mainly grass, switching to cacti and forbs when grass is scarce. Cougars, coyotes and bobcats prey on it.

nodes.name: Deer mouse
nodes.desc: The most-recorded mammal near the park. A small seed-eating rodent that many snakes, scavengers and canids eat.

nodes.name: Desert woodrat
nodes.desc: A pack-rat of rocky desert slopes that feeds on cacti, juniper and other plants.

nodes.name: Clark's nutcracker
nodes.desc: A crow-family bird that harvests pine seeds and caches them, so it helps spread pines.

nodes.name: White-tailed antelope squirrel
nodes.desc: An omnivorous ground squirrel active in desert heat. GloBI records show it eating mice.

nodes.name: Bullsnake
nodes.desc: A large constrictor that hunts rodents, ground squirrels and birds.

nodes.name: Great Basin rattlesnake
nodes.desc: A pit viper that ambushes rodents and lizards on rocky slopes.

nodes.name: Common raven
nodes.desc: A clever omnivore and scavenger, the most-recorded bird near the park.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Soars over the canyons and feeds mainly on carrion, finding it by smell.

nodes.name: Mountain lion
nodes.desc: The main large predator of deer and bighorn in the canyon country.

nodes.name: Coyote
nodes.desc: An adaptable hunter of rodents and young deer that also eats carrion.

nodes.name: Soil microbes and fungi
nodes.desc: Break down dead plants and animals, returning nutrients to the thin desert soil.
